subject: Energy
title: Electricity as an Energy Carrier
description: A micro-lesson that makes Electricity as an Energy Carrier usable.

hook.text: Electricity isn't a source of energy—it's a carrier, a way to move energy from where it's made to where it's needed.

buildup.text: Power plants convert fuel into electricity—then wires deliver it at near light speed to homes and factories.

discovery.text: Electricity is versatile—it can become light, heat, motion, or computation with very high conversion efficiency.

twist.text: About 5% of electricity is lost during transmission—resistance in power lines converts current into waste heat.

climax.text: High-voltage transmission reduces losses—that's why power lines carry hundreds of thousands of volts across the country.

punchline.text: Electricity doesn't make energy—it just delivers it.

quiz.question: Why are power lines operated at high voltage?
